agents_spawned.task_context: Refine issue #1059: Implement overseer agent for pipeline health monitoring. This is a large feature that adds a new always-on agent role (overseer) that monitors pipeline health, detects stalls/loops/failures, uses Haiku for log analysis, and escalates to humans. The issue has very detailed requirements already - your job is to: 1) Identify any gaps, ambiguities, or conflicts in the requirements. 2) Assess the scope and suggest phasing if needed (the issue already defers token budget tracking). 3) Validate the infrastructure changes list against the actual codebase - check orchestrator/models.py, shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py, orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py, orchestrator/routes/coordinator.py, orchestrator/container_spawner.py to confirm the listed changes are accurate and complete. 4) Check for dependencies - issues #1027 and #1028 are listed. Verify they exist and their status. 5) Identify any missing requirements (e.g., how does overseer know pipeline is complete to shut down? What happens if overseer container itself crashes? Config for Haiku API endpoint/model?). 6) Write refined requirements to .egg-state/drafts/. Focus on making requirements implementable - flag anything that needs clarification before coding begins.

Review the refinement output for issue #1059: Implement overseer agent for pipeline health monitoring. This is a new always-on agent that monitors pipeline health across all coordinator-spawned pipelines. Review the refiner's output in .egg-state/drafts/ for: 1) Completeness - are all requirements from the issue captured and refined? 2) Feasibility - are the proposed changes realistic given the codebase architecture? 3) Risk - what are the highest-risk aspects? (e.g., auto-spawning on every pipeline, Haiku API dependency, container config changes) 4) Scope - is this properly scoped for a single implementation cycle or should it be broken into multiple issues? 5) Testability - can each requirement be verified? 6) Security - the overseer has broad read access to all agent logs and infrastructure. Any concerns? Review thoroughly and provide actionable feedback.

Review the agent design for issue #1059: Implement overseer agent for pipeline health monitoring. Focus on the agent architecture aspects: 1) Agent role design - does the OVERSEER role definition fit cleanly into the existing AgentRole enum and role definition patterns? Check shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py for existing patterns. 2) Container configuration - the overseer has no repo mount (like coordinator) but needs orchestrator/gateway/GitHub API access. Verify this is consistent with how coordinator containers are configured. 3) Spawn lifecycle - auto-spawn with coordinator, run until pipeline completes. How does this interact with existing container lifecycle management? 4) CLAUDE.md instructions - the overseer needs a prompt section similar to the coordinator. Is the proposed instruction set sufficient for an autonomous monitoring agent? 5) Haiku integration - calling Claude API directly from within the agent container. Is this pattern established elsewhere? What about API key management? 6) Message bus interaction - the overseer reads all messages but only sends redirects/nudges. Is this the right access pattern? 7) Coordinator interaction - overseer monitors coordinator but cannot restart it. Is the escalation path clear? Review the design and flag any architectural concerns.
